provenance.note: These reviews were produced from earlier contended or rejected timing diagnostics. They remain useful planning input, but do not satisfy the authoritative repeated-warm review gate for the current source fingerprint. The exact source fingerprint was not retained with the candidate set, so it is deliberately null rather than inferred.

t_b0_repro_build_runquota_daemon.justification: The test launches the real RunQuota daemon and drives a repro build through its socket, so process startup and IPC are part of the contract under test.
t_b0_repro_build_runquota_daemon.followUp: Keep it in the integration lane and publish its daemon-start and build phases separately so later milestones can optimize without dropping the real-daemon assertion.

t_b1_apps_action_cache_hit.justification: A cold action followed by a cache-hit build is required to prove the apps collection reuses the recorded action result.
t_b1_apps_action_cache_hit.followUp: Retain both builds but reuse a graph-owned apps fixture and record cold versus hit timing independently.

t_b1_repro_build_apps_collection.justification: This exercises collection selection through the production repro CLI and build engine rather than only inspecting collection metadata in process.
t_b1_repro_build_apps_collection.followUp: Move the project setup into a graph-owned fixture while preserving the end-to-end collection build and output checks.

t_b2_helper_invalidation.justification: The test must build, mutate a helper input, and rebuild to verify invalidation propagates through the real action graph.
t_b2_helper_invalidation.followUp: Share the initial graph-owned fixture with the adjacent helper tests and keep the mutation/rebuild assertion isolated.

t_b3_test_execute_edge_cache_hit.justification: Two executions are intrinsic to proving that the test-execute edge is served from its cache on the second run.
t_b3_test_execute_edge_cache_hit.followUp: Expose per-edge cache timing and reuse the prepared fixture rather than recreating the whole project.

t_b3_test_invalidation_rebuilds_repro.justification: The regression requires a before/after build around a source mutation to show that the repro target is rebuilt instead of incorrectly reused.
t_b3_test_invalidation_rebuilds_repro.followUp: Retain the two-phase assertion but make the initial target a graph-owned artifact shared by the B3 integration group.

t_d1_pythonunittest_resolves_in_path_mod.justification: PATH-mode resolution is a subprocess and environment contract; an in-process lookup would not cover the production tool-provisioning path.
t_d1_pythonunittest_resolves_in_path_mod.followUp: Use a prebuilt graph-owned Python unittest fixture and keep only the production PATH-resolution invocation in this test.

t_d2_cross_project_selector_recognised.justification: The test creates project recipes and invokes repro so the provider graph is compiled and evaluated before the cross-project selector can be checked.
t_d2_cross_project_selector_recognised.followUp: Prebuild the provider pair as a graph-owned fixture and leave selector recognition and diagnostics in the runtime test.

t_d5_collection_member_selector.justification: Collection-member selection is tested by compiling/evaluating a synthetic project and then driving the production CLI over several selectors.
t_d5_collection_member_selector.followUp: Publish the collection provider as a reusable graph artifact and split selector cases from fixture construction.

t_e2e_local_reprobuild_project_build.justification: The local-build-engine capstone compiles its helper/project material during the test and then performs a full production build.
t_e2e_local_reprobuild_project_build.followUp: Move helper compilation to declared test-build edges while retaining the end-to-end local project build.

t_e2e_native_shell_hooks.justification: Real Bash, Zsh, and Fish startup plus the Nix-managed-file refusal path are the behavior under test and cannot be represented by formatter-only unit checks.
t_e2e_native_shell_hooks.followUp: Keep the real-shell gate exclusive, but reuse one prepared dev-env fixture across shells and report each shell case separately.

t_e2e_repro_dev_sessions.justification: The suite starts real supervised services and a watch process to verify up, down, event, and cleanup semantics across process boundaries.
t_e2e_repro_dev_sessions.followUp: Retain the live-process coverage in an exclusive lane and factor reusable service fixtures into graph-owned artifacts.

t_b2_helpers_built_by_engine.justification: The assertion specifically requires the build engine, rather than the test body, to produce and consume helper artifacts.
t_b2_helpers_built_by_engine.followUp: Share the graph-owned helper target with other B2 tests and keep the ownership/provenance assertions here.

t_build_progress_modes.justification: Several progress presentation modes rebuild equivalent fixture state, so repeated provider and graph setup dominates the formatting assertions.
t_build_progress_modes.followUp: Prepare one graph snapshot and exercise each progress renderer against it without rerunning unchanged setup.

t_d1_buildnimunittest_resolves_in_path_m.justification: The production buildNimUnittest path compiles a Nim test fixture before PATH-mode execution can be verified.
t_d1_buildnimunittest_resolves_in_path_m.followUp: Declare the fixture binary as a test-build edge and retain only PATH selection and execution checks at runtime.

t_client_cli_prefix_substitute.justification: CLI-prefix substitution crosses the binary-cache client protocol and real subprocess boundary, which is the compatibility surface being protected.
t_client_cli_prefix_substitute.followUp: Keep the protocol integration test but share the cache/client fixture and separate each prefix case in timing output.

t_dev_env_allow.justification: The allow-policy cases repeatedly prepare equivalent dev-environment project and policy state around small authorization differences.
t_dev_env_allow.followUp: Reuse one prepared provider artifact and reset only the allow database or policy input between cases.

t_dev_env_artifact.justification: Producing the dev-env artifact requires compiling and evaluating the fixture provider through the production graph.
t_dev_env_artifact.followUp: Make the provider output a graph-owned fixture and keep artifact contents, provenance, and invalidation assertions in the test.

t_e2e_codetracer_build_subset_without_tu.justification: The test evaluates a pinned CodeTracer checkout and builds a representative subset to prove the Tup-free path, making the external product fixture the dominant cost.
t_e2e_codetracer_build_subset_without_tu.followUp: Keep the pinned capstone but isolate it in the CodeTracer integration shard and publish reusable provider/build artifacts.

t_a3_p2_cli_substitute.justification: The A3/P2 check intentionally exercises CLI substitution across producer, cache, and consumer process boundaries.
t_a3_p2_cli_substitute.followUp: Retain the cross-process contract while reusing a prepared producer/cache fixture across substitution variants.

t_e2e_codetracer_dev_environment_slice.justification: A pinned multi-repository CodeTracer workspace is evaluated to validate the real development-environment slice, so fixture breadth is intentional and expensive.
t_e2e_codetracer_dev_environment_slice.followUp: Run this in the pinned CodeTracer shard and reuse its provider artifact with the adjacent subset and in-place tests.

t_e2e_dev_env_deactivate_round_trip.justification: Most cases validate in-process environment-diff behavior, while the end-to-end case repeats full dev-env provider setup already covered by neighboring tests.
t_e2e_dev_env_deactivate_round_trip.followUp: Consolidate the synthetic cases into a pure-unit binary and leave one graph-owned end-to-end round trip.

t_cross_repo_nim_library_src_threaded_on.justification: The SC11 regression is only observable after compiling pinned producer and consumer providers and then building the cross-repository Nim consumer.
t_cross_repo_nim_library_src_threaded_on.followUp: Publish producer/provider outputs as graph-owned artifacts while retaining the exact consumer-path and runtime assertions.

t_e2e_dev_env_export_bash.justification: Small Bash formatter cases share a binary with a full provider-backed export, so the integration setup inflates the entire test binary.
t_e2e_dev_env_export_bash.followUp: Move formatter cases to a consolidated pure-unit suite and retain one Bash export against a reusable dev-env fixture.

t_e2e_dev_env_deactivate_tampered.justification: Unit-level tamper and formatter checks are bundled with two provider-backed end-to-end cases that independently recreate similar dev-env state.
t_e2e_dev_env_deactivate_tampered.followUp: Consolidate pure tamper checks and reuse one prepared artifact for the manifest-hash and artifact-tamper cases.

t_e2e_dev_env_export_fish.justification: The Fish formatter assertions are inexpensive, but sharing the binary with a full provider-backed export adds repeated integration setup.
t_e2e_dev_env_export_fish.followUp: Consolidate formatter coverage with other shell formatters and keep one reusable-fixture Fish export gate.

t_e2e_dev_env_edge_cache.justification: No-op reuse and observed-input invalidation require repeated production CLI runs against the same edge cache.
t_e2e_dev_env_edge_cache.followUp: Retain the stateful sequence but create the provider artifact through a shared graph-owned fixture.

t_e2e_develop_overrides_activity.justification: Each override change causes production provider compilation/evaluation so the resulting activity and artifact rebinding can be observed.
t_e2e_develop_overrides_activity.followUp: Prebuild stable providers and limit runtime compilation to the override whose invalidation behavior is under test.

t_e2e_dev_env_performance_gates.justification: The suite deliberately measures real activation and changed-input paths, so repeated production CLI calls are the performance contract rather than incidental work.
t_e2e_dev_env_performance_gates.followUp: Keep it as an exclusive benchmark gate and emit activation phases separately for trend analysis.

t_e2e_hooks_shell_direnv.justification: Real direnv allow, exec, hook installation, conflict, no-op, and uninstall behavior spans external process and filesystem contracts.
t_e2e_hooks_shell_direnv.followUp: Preserve the real-direnv coverage but share one prepared project and split lifecycle cases for sharding.

t_e2e_profile_modules.justification: Profile-module behavior is verified by compiling generated profiles and modules through the production helper.
t_e2e_profile_modules.followUp: Declare representative profile binaries as graph-owned artifacts and keep runtime work only for invalidation-specific cases.

t_e2e_provider_dev_env_introspection.justification: The test compiles/evaluates a provider fixture before inspecting its dev-env diagnostics and observed reads.
t_e2e_provider_dev_env_introspection.followUp: Reuse a graph-owned provider artifact across introspection cases and preserve the observability assertions.

t_e2e_m51_dsl_stdlib_file_ops.justification: The M51 gate compiles a DSL provider and executes real filesystem actions to validate the standard-library operation contract.
t_e2e_m51_dsl_stdlib_file_ops.followUp: Prebuild the provider fixture and time action execution separately from provider compilation.

t_e2e_repro_profile_compile_via_action.justification: The production action intentionally compiles a profile binary, and that compiler invocation dominates the end-to-end check.
t_e2e_repro_profile_compile_via_action.followUp: Keep one action-owned compile gate and share its source graph/nimcache with related profile tests where semantics allow.

t_e2e_repro_exec_shell.justification: Multiple exec and shell cases repeatedly invoke the same provider-backed dev environment while varying exit status, cwd, or presentation behavior.
t_e2e_repro_exec_shell.followUp: Prepare one dev-env artifact and reuse it across exec/shell cases, retaining isolated subprocess assertions.

t_e2e_repro_profile_compile.justification: This test invokes the production profile compiler on generated sources, so compiler startup and module compilation are intrinsic costs.
t_e2e_repro_profile_compile.followUp: Use shared nimcache/source artifacts and keep separate success, invalidation, and diagnostic measurements.

t_e2e_shell_hook_cd_activate_deactivate.justification: The test builds a counting shim and then drives a real Bash cd/activate/deactivate lifecycle through the production executable.
t_e2e_shell_hook_cd_activate_deactivate.followUp: Declare the counting shim as a test-build artifact and retain the real shell lifecycle assertions.

t_e2e_shell_hook_noop_io_bounded.justification: The no-op I/O bound is only meaningful under the real monitor shim and production shell-hook subprocess path.
t_e2e_shell_hook_noop_io_bounded.followUp: Keep the monitored integration gate exclusive and reuse graph-owned monitor tools instead of preparing them per test.

t_e2e_repro_watch_multiple_named_targets.justification: Multiple named targets, filesystem changes, watch cycles, and cleanup must be exercised through a live watcher to protect routing behavior.
t_e2e_repro_watch_multiple_named_targets.followUp: Retain the live-watch gate and move static fixture/provider preparation to graph-owned artifacts.

t_e2e_shell_hook_realistic_workload.justification: Forty prompt invocations are deliberate: the test protects the cumulative no-op fast-path budget under a realistic shell workload.
t_e2e_shell_hook_realistic_workload.followUp: Keep it in the performance lane, report per-prompt distributions, and avoid weakening the 40-prompt assertion.

t_integration_provider_fragment_refresh_.justification: Provider fragments are compiled, refreshed after source changes, and pruned to validate lifecycle behavior across real artifacts.
t_integration_provider_fragment_refresh_.followUp: Declare helper/provider binaries as graph-owned test artifacts and preserve refresh/prune transitions at runtime.

t_integration_stow_gnu_package_layout.justification: GNU Stow compatibility depends on a real staged package layout, filesystem links, and uninstall behavior rather than an in-memory model.
t_integration_stow_gnu_package_layout.followUp: Retain the filesystem integration gate and reuse a prepared package tree across layout cases.

t_integration_reprobuild_sessions_share_.justification: The test prepares helper executables and launches concurrent reprobuild sessions against a real RunQuota daemon to verify shared accounting.
t_integration_reprobuild_sessions_share_.followUp: Move helpers to test-build edges and keep only daemon/session concurrency in the runtime phase.

t_local_daemons_control_plane_m0.justification: M0 checks the public daemon/store CLI surface and direct-mode parity through the production executable and real fixture build.
t_local_daemons_control_plane_m0.followUp: Keep the surface gate but reuse its direct-mode project artifact with later control-plane milestones.

t_local_daemons_control_plane_m10.justification: The binary covers development self-restart, state preservation, source-image replacement, and platform staging with repeated daemon lifecycles.
t_local_daemons_control_plane_m10.followUp: Split restart and state-corruption scenarios into shardable cases sharing one graph-owned daemon image.

t_local_daemons_control_plane_m4.justification: Parity, RunQuota use, active/recent sessions, and cancellation each start substantial daemon/build fixtures inside one binary.
t_local_daemons_control_plane_m4.followUp: Separate parity, quota, and cancellation cases while sharing graph-owned daemon and project fixtures.

t_local_daemons_control_plane_m3.justification: The flag matrix performs many complete builds and the cancellation case adds a live daemon/client workflow in the same suite.
t_local_daemons_control_plane_m3.followUp: Move the pure flag-validation cases to a lighter table test and retain one direct/auto/require integration matrix plus cancellation gate.

t_local_daemons_control_plane_m6.justification: Warm no-op and direct/daemon incremental-record parity require repeated real builds against a live daemon and shared cache.
t_local_daemons_control_plane_m6.followUp: Keep the benchmark sequence intact and publish its setup, cold, no-op, and changed-action phases separately.

t_local_daemons_control_plane_m5.justification: Two-watch, detach/reattach, platform watcher, and direct-watch scenarios each run long-lived daemon/watch processes in one suite.
t_local_daemons_control_plane_m5.followUp: Split watcher scenarios into exclusive shardable binaries and reuse a graph-owned watch project fixture.

t_local_daemons_control_plane_m7.justification: Stats capture and hot-path flushing are persistence and timing contracts that require a live daemon and several production builds.
t_local_daemons_control_plane_m7.followUp: Retain both stateful sequences but share daemon startup and project setup, reporting flush phases separately.

t_local_daemons_control_plane_m11.justification: Unavailable, stale, protocol-mismatch, fallback, output-parity, and watch-default scenarios span many complete daemon and build lifecycles.
t_local_daemons_control_plane_m11.followUp: Split recovery, parity, and watch rollout into independently shardable binaries with shared fake-daemon and project artifacts.

t_m54_verified_tarball_profile.justification: The M54 gate verifies a real tarball profile, extraction, hash/provenance handling, and resulting profile behavior across filesystem boundaries.
t_m54_verified_tarball_profile.followUp: Keep one verified-tarball capstone and make the archive/profile inputs reusable graph-owned fixtures.

t_local_daemons_control_plane_m8.justification: Ranking, snapshot comparison, and graph-analysis views independently start daemons and build projects inside one integration binary.
t_local_daemons_control_plane_m8.followUp: Split the three analysis surfaces and share one captured stats/graph fixture where freshness semantics permit.

t_m9r22b_3_apply_cli.justification: Each disk CLI case parses and compiles generated hardware/profile source before dry-run apply, mount, or unmount behavior is asserted.
t_m9r22b_3_apply_cli.followUp: Compile the single- and multi-disk profiles once as graph-owned fixtures and reuse them across CLI gating cases.

t_nested_topology_full_pipeline_without_.justification: The test constructs and evaluates a nested multi-project topology through the complete provider and build pipeline.
t_nested_topology_full_pipeline_without_.followUp: Publish the nested providers as reusable graph artifacts while preserving the no-org-root end-to-end assertion.

t_peer_cache_bearssl_200_peer_tls_conver.justification: The intentional 200-peer fleet creates 200 keypairs/certificates, performs signed dissemination, and waits for full SWIM convergence.
t_peer_cache_bearssl_200_peer_tls_conver.followUp: Keep the 200-peer scale gate in a dedicated shard and add a smaller fast correctness fixture without reducing this scale assertion.

t_peer_cache_bearssl_tls_partition_recov.justification: The test converges a 200-peer TLS-mode fleet, kills 20 peers, and waits through the real suspect/confirm/remove recovery pipeline.
t_peer_cache_bearssl_tls_partition_recov.followUp: Keep the full recovery scale test in a dedicated shard and report convergence and recovery phases independently.

t_nim_package_path_handling.justification: Three production builds and dependency mutations are required to verify path generation, early cut-off, and invalidation; provider compilation dominates.
t_nim_package_path_handling.followUp: Reuse prebuilt sibling/provider fixtures and retain the three-state cache/invalidation sequence.

t_project_extension_adds_edges_to_origin.justification: The extension and original project recipes are compiled/evaluated before the merged target table can be observed through the CLI.
t_project_extension_adds_edges_to_origin.followUp: Declare the provider pair as a graph-owned fixture and keep the merged-edge assertion at runtime.

t_project_dsl_build_action_payload.justification: The cases only encode/decode small in-memory action payloads, so a long runtime points to heavy repro_project_dsl initialization rather than test scope.
t_project_dsl_build_action_payload.followUp: Decouple payload codecs from the full DSL initialization path and consolidate version-compatibility cases into a lightweight unit binary.

t_project_extension_inert_when_absent_an.justification: Absent and present phases each compile/evaluate project providers so automatic extension discovery can be compared.
t_project_extension_inert_when_absent_an.followUp: Reuse the original provider artifact and compile only the extension delta between phases.

t_project_interface_artifact_import_mode.justification: The test explicitly compiles provider, thin-consumer, and source-consumer fixtures to validate artifact import and invalidation modes.
t_project_interface_artifact_import_mode.followUp: Move fixture compilation into declared test-build graph edges and retain mode/fingerprint assertions over their outputs.

t_project_extension_target_rehomed_and_t.justification: Absent, present, qualified-target, and removed phases repeatedly compile/evaluate providers to verify graph cache invalidation and target re-homing.
t_project_extension_target_rehomed_and_t.followUp: Share provider outputs across phases and rebuild only the extension signature delta under test.

t_repro_build_test_aggregate_builds_ever.justification: The assertion intentionally asks the production aggregate to traverse and build the complete declared test graph, making suite size its fixture.
t_repro_build_test_aggregate_builds_ever.followUp: Keep one complete aggregate audit but run it once per build pipeline rather than inside every timed test execution.

t_repro_build_unknown_target_diagnostic.justification: The production CLI loads and evaluates a fixture project before it can emit the unknown-target diagnostic and candidate list.
t_repro_build_unknown_target_diagnostic.followUp: Use a graph-owned lowered fixture and keep only diagnostic resolution/rendering in the runtime test.

t_repro_list_targets_lists_implicit_and_.justification: Listing implicit and explicit targets goes through production provider compilation and graph lowering for the fixture project.
t_repro_list_targets_lists_implicit_and_.followUp: Prebuild the provider/lowered graph and retain CLI target enumeration and attribution assertions.

t_e2e_codetracer_in_place_project_file.justification: The capstone builds the real pinned CodeTracer project in place across its multi-repository workspace and validates deliberate missing-edge behavior.
t_e2e_codetracer_in_place_project_file.followUp: Keep this exact pinned capstone in an exclusive CodeTracer shard and reuse its immutable provider artifacts across cold/warm phases.

t_repro_watch_unknown_target_diagnostic.justification: The watch command compiles/evaluates the project graph before validating an unknown target, even though no watch cycle can start.
t_repro_watch_unknown_target_diagnostic.followUp: Share a lowered fixture with the build diagnostic test and retain watch-specific wording/exit assertions.

t_repro_test_runner_parallel_n_workers.justification: The test compiles twelve parallel fixtures plus the exact production-basename exclusive fixtures at runtime before measuring overlap.
t_repro_test_runner_parallel_n_workers.followUp: Declare all fixture binaries as graph-owned test-build artifacts; keep exact overlap, count, and exclusivity assertions unchanged.

t_sc_executable_producer_edge_spliced_an.justification: Producer and consumer providers plus the executable edge must be compiled/built to prove splicing and PATH exposure end to end.
t_sc_executable_producer_edge_spliced_an.followUp: Reuse graph-owned producer artifacts and keep consumer PATH/provenance assertions in the runtime phase.

t_repro_test_runner_aggregate_exit_code.justification: Twenty protocol-aware fixture binaries are compiled for each aggregate and fail-fast scenario before exact exit/count behavior is tested.
t_repro_test_runner_aggregate_exit_code.followUp: Build the 20 fixtures once through declared graph edges and reuse them for both default and fail-fast runs without weakening exact counts.

t_sc_develop_mode_consumes_sibling_exe_a.justification: Develop-mode producer/consumer providers and both executable and library artifacts are compiled from sibling source to validate real consumption.
t_sc_develop_mode_consumes_sibling_exe_a.followUp: Publish producer artifacts through graph-owned edges and preserve develop-mode source selection assertions.

t_sc_library_producer_edge_spliced_throu.justification: The library producer and consumer are compiled so auxiliary path/channel propagation can be checked through the actual build graph.
t_sc_library_producer_edge_spliced_throu.followUp: Prebuild the producer library/provider and retain exact auxiliary-channel and consumer-link assertions.

t_sc_producer_exports_typed_cli_contract.justification: A producer provider and downstream consumer are compiled to validate the typed CLI contract across workspace boundaries.
t_sc_producer_exports_typed_cli_contract.followUp: Use graph-owned provider artifacts and keep typed argument/schema compatibility checks end to end.

t_smoke_module_imports.justification: Several generated profile/module graphs are compiled through compileProfileBinary, including success, composition, diagnostics, and digest cases.
t_smoke_module_imports.followUp: Separate pure source-discovery/digest cases and share nimcache/artifacts across the remaining representative compile cases.

t_sc_capstone_reprobuild_runquota_and_li.justification: The capstone builds a cross-repository library consumer under develop and lock-pinned modes, runs RunQuota, and includes a deliberate missing-edge negative control.
t_sc_capstone_reprobuild_runquota_and_li.followUp: Keep the exact capstone exclusive, but reuse immutable producer/provider artifacts and report each mode and negative control separately.

test_kcmutils_source.justification: The test only checks static recipe URL, hash, artifact, and version fields; its runtime is disproportionate to these in-memory assertions.
test_kcmutils_source.followUp: Load recipe descriptors through a lightweight metadata path and consolidate source-recipe smoke tests by dependency shape.

t_sc_lock_pinned_fetches_and_builds_sibl.justification: The lock-pinned scenario fetches, compiles, and builds an immutable sibling project to validate source resolution and consumption.
t_sc_lock_pinned_fetches_and_builds_sibl.followUp: Keep one exact lock-pinned integration gate and cache its immutable fetch/provider artifacts between test phases.

test_m25_adapter_preference_text_macro_p.justification: The adapter-preference parity test compiles generated macro/text fixtures so compile-time selection matches runtime semantics.
test_m25_adapter_preference_text_macro_p.followUp: Declare generated adapter fixtures as graph-owned compile artifacts and compare their outputs without compiling in the test body.

test_kwin_source.justification: Static KWin recipe metadata and artifact assertions should be cheap; the observed time comes from importing and initializing the full project DSL/recipe graph.
test_kwin_source.followUp: Expose lightweight recipe metadata and consolidate equivalent source-recipe smoke cases.

test_plasma5support_source.justification: Two static fetch/artifact assertions take far longer than their logic warrants because full recipe/DSL initialization is paid.
test_plasma5support_source.followUp: Test the descriptor through a lightweight metadata API and merge it with the related Plasma source-recipe smoke suite.

test_plasma_framework_source.justification: The suite checks fixed URL, hash, flags, artifact, and version fields; expensive DSL/recipe initialization dominates the small assertions.
test_plasma_framework_source.followUp: Separate recipe metadata from full provider initialization and consolidate with neighboring Plasma descriptor tests.

t_sc_typed_cross_project_consumption_bot.justification: Typed cross-project consumption is built and executed in both develop and lock-pinned modes, requiring complete producer/consumer provider pipelines.
t_sc_typed_cross_project_consumption_bot.followUp: Retain both modes as one compatibility capstone but reuse immutable producer artifacts and shard it from faster SC checks.

test_plasma_workspace_source.justification: The test performs only static recipe metadata and artifact checks, so the long duration reflects heavyweight DSL/recipe initialization.
test_plasma_workspace_source.followUp: Provide a lightweight recipe-descriptor path and consolidate Plasma source smoke tests into one binary.
